@SPRINT3-RULES.md , gh is not installed.

Lets work on https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/issues/158
We have the pr open at https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/pull/177, but have gotten feedback that we do not have enough test coverage from SonarQube "one 29.2% of the 80% required" on the new code, and from Gitar

```
Code Review: Adds multi-line code comment ranges in Files changed, with server-side validation and range-aware invalidation, but the change has an open issue. The AC11 e2e check can pass on a stale toast left over from AC15, so it does not verify that old-to-new range selections are refused. Close that toast before the AC11 step, assert a new toast appears, and confirm the selection was cleared.

1. ⚠️ Quality: AC11 e2e check passes on the toast still showing from AC15
   Files: tests/e2e/pr-suggest-change.test.ts:149-154, tests/e2e/pr-suggest-change.test.ts:164-167, web_src/js/features/repo-diff-range.ts:45-50

   Error toasts never close on their own (`duration: -1` in `web_src/js/modules/toast.ts`). `showToast` also has `preventDuplicates` on by default, so a second toast with the same level and message does not get a new element; it only bumps the counter on the existing one. AC15 already leaves a visible toast with exactly `message`. So when the AC11 step clicks old line 2 and then shift-clicks new line 4, `page.getByText(message).last()` finds that same AC15 toast and passes even if `selectLine` never refuses the old-to-new range. That assertion cannot fail for the behavior it is meant to test.

   Fix: close the AC15 toast (or check that no toast is visible) before the AC11 step, then assert that a toast appears again. Also check that the selection was cleared, e.g. `tr.range-selected` has count 0.

   Fix (Close the AC15 toast first, then check that the refusal shows a new toast and clears the selection):
   // AC11: old side to new side is refused with a message
   await page.locator('.toastify .toast-close').click();
   await expect(page.getByText(message)).toHaveCount(0);
   await lineNum('old', 2).click();
   await lineNum('new', 4).click({modifiers: ['Shift']});
   await expect(page.getByText(message)).toBeVisible();
   await expect(page.locator('tr.range-selected')).toHaveCount(0);
```

416	+	"testing"

419	+)
420	+
421	+func TestRangeChanged(t *testing.T) {
422	+	original := []string{"l3", "l4", "l5"} // a comment on lines 3-5
423	+	cases := []struct {
424	+		name    string
425	+		content string
426	+		start   int64
427	+		changed bool
428	+	}{
429	+		{"unchanged", "l1\nl2\nl3\nl4\nl5\nl6\n", 3, false},
430	+		{"first line changed", "l1\nl2\nX\nl4\nl5\nl6\n", 3, true},
431	+		{"middle line changed", "l1\nl2\nl3\nX\nl5\nl6\n", 3, true},
432	+		{"last line changed", "l1\nl2\nl3\nl4\nX\nl6\n", 3, true},
433	+		{"only a line after the range changed", "l1\nl2\nl3\nl4\nl5\nX\n", 3, false},
434	+		{"range ends on the last line, no final newline", "l1\nl2\nl3\nl4\nl5", 3, false},
435	+		{"last line deleted", "l1\nl2\nl3\nl4\n", 3, true},
436	+		{"file deleted", "", 3, true},
437	+	}
438	+	for _, c := range cases {
439	+		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
440	+			assert.Equal(t, c.changed, rangeChanged(original, c.content, c.start))
441	+		})
442	+	}
443	+}

512	@@ -0,0 +1,32 @@
513	+import {collectRangeRows} from './repo-diff-range.ts';
514	+
515	+// a unified diff: new-side lines carry data-line-num on td.lines-num-new, removed lines have it empty
516	+function row(cls: string, newLine = '') {
517	+  return `<tr class="${cls}"><td class="lines-num lines-num-new" data-line-num="${newLine}"></td></tr>`;
518	+}
519	+
520	+function rowsOf(html: string) {
521	+  document.body.innerHTML = `<table><tbody>${html}</tbody></table>`;
522	+  return Array.from(document.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('tr'));
523	+}
524	+
525	+const lineNums = (rows: HTMLElement[] | null) => rows?.map((tr) => tr.querySelector('td')!.getAttribute('data-line-num'));
526	+
527	+test('collectRangeRows', () => {
528	+  const trs = rowsOf(row('same-code', '18') + row('del-code') + row('add-code', '19') + row('add-comment') + row('same-code', '20'));
529	+  // #158 AC1: lines 18-20, skipping the removed line and the comment row
530	+  expect(lineNums(collectRangeRows(trs[0], trs[4]))).toEqual(['18', '19', '20']);
531	+  // #158 AC2: an upward selection gives the same range
532	+  expect(lineNums(collectRangeRows(trs[4], trs[0]))).toEqual(['18', '19', '20']);
533	+  // #158 AC3: one line
534	+  expect(lineNums(collectRangeRows(trs[2], trs[2]))).toEqual(['19']);
535	+});
536	+
537	+test('collectRangeRows refuses a range outside one hunk', () => {
538	+  // #158 AC10: crossing a hunk header
539	+  const trs = rowsOf(row('same-code', '18') + row('tag-code') + row('same-code', '40'));
540	+  expect(collectRangeRows(trs[0], trs[2])).toBeNull();
541	+  // #158 AC10: expanded context lines
542	+  const expanded = rowsOf(row('same-code line-expanded', '17') + row('same-code', '18'));
543	+  expect(collectRangeRows(expanded[0], expanded[1])).toBeNull();
544	+});
545	diff --git a/web_src/js/features/repo-diff-range.ts b/web_src/js/features/repo-diff-range.ts
546	new file mode 100644
547	index 0000000000..62a1bdbb90
548	--- /dev/null
549	+++ b/web_src/js/features/repo-diff-range.ts
550	@@ -0,0 +1,64 @@
551	+import {addDelegatedEventListener} from '../utils/dom.ts';
552	+import {showErrorToast} from '../modules/toast.ts';
553	+
554	+let anchor: {tr: HTMLElement, side: string} | null = null;
555	+let selected: HTMLElement[] = [];
556	+
557	+function newLineNum(tr: Element): number {
558	+  return Number(tr.querySelector('td.lines-num-new')?.getAttribute('data-line-num') || 0);
559	+}
560	+
561	+/** the new-side rows from `a` to `b` in either order, or null when they aren't in one hunk */
562	+export function collectRangeRows(a: HTMLElement, b: HTMLElement): HTMLElement[] | null {
563	+  const [first, last] = a.compareDocumentPosition(b) & Node.DOCUMENT_POSITION_PRECEDING ? [b, a] : [a, b];
564	+  const rows: HTMLElement[] = [];
565	+  for (let tr: Element | null = first; tr; tr = tr.nextElementSibling) {
566	+    // a hunk header, or expanded context which belongs to no hunk
567	+    if (tr.classList.contains('tag-code') || tr.classList.contains('line-expanded')) return null;
568	+    if (newLineNum(tr)) rows.push(tr as HTMLElement); // skips removed lines and comment rows
569	+    if (tr === last) return rows;
570	+  }
571	+  return null; // `last` isn't after `first` in this file
572	+}
573	+
574	+function setSelected(rows: HTMLElement[]) {
575	+  for (const tr of selected) tr.classList.remove('range-selected');
576	+  selected = rows;
577	+  for (const tr of selected) tr.classList.add('range-selected');
578	+}
579	+
580	+/** the selected range, when `tr` is its last row and it has more than one line */
581	+export function getSelectedRange(tr: Element): {rows: HTMLElement[], start: number, end: number} | null {
582	+  if (selected.length < 2 || selected.at(-1) !== tr) return null;
583	+  return {rows: selected, start: newLineNum(selected[0]), end: newLineNum(tr)};
584	+}
585	+
586	+function selectLine(td: HTMLElement, extend: boolean) {
587	+  const tr = td.closest('tr')!;
588	+  const side = td.classList.contains('lines-num-new') ? 'right' : 'left';
589	+  if (!extend || !anchor) {
590	+    anchor = {tr, side};
591	+    setSelected(side === 'right' ? [tr] : []);
592	+    return;
593	+  }
594	+  window.getSelection()?.removeAllRanges();
595	+  const rows = anchor.side === 'right' && side === 'right' ? collectRangeRows(anchor.tr, tr) : null;
596	+  if (!rows) {
597	+    anchor = null;
598	+    setSelected([]);
599	+    showErrorToast(td.closest('[data-range-invalid]')!.getAttribute('data-range-invalid')!);
600	+    return;
601	+  }
602	+  setSelected(rows);
603	+}
604	+
605	+// click a line number to start a range, shift-click another to end it; Enter / Shift+Enter do the same from the keyboard
606	+export function initDiffRangeSelect() {
607	+  const selector = '[data-range-invalid] td.lines-num[data-line-num]:not([data-line-num=""])';
608	+  addDelegatedEventListener(document, 'click', selector, (td, e: MouseEvent) => selectLine(td, e.shiftKey));
609	+  addDelegatedEventListener(document, 'keydown', selector, (td, e: KeyboardEvent) => {
610	+    if (e.key !== 'Enter') return;
611	+    e.preventDefault();
612	+    selectLine(td, e.shiftKey);
613	+  });
614	+}

func TestRenderConversation(t *testing.T) {
	unittest.PrepareTestEnv(t)

	pr, _ := issues_model.GetPullRequestByID(t.Context(), 2)
	_ = pr.LoadIssue(t.Context())
	_ = pr.Issue.LoadPoster(t.Context())
	_ = pr.Issue.LoadRepo(t.Context())

	run := func(name string, cb func(t *testing.T, ctx *context.Context, resp *httptest.ResponseRecorder)) {
		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
			ctx, resp := contexttest.MockContext(t, "/", contexttest.MockContextOption{Render: templates.PageRenderer()})
			contexttest.LoadUser(t, ctx, pr.Issue.PosterID)
			contexttest.LoadRepo(t, ctx, pr.BaseRepoID)
			contexttest.LoadGitRepo(t, ctx)
			defer ctx.Repo.GitRepo.Close()
			cb(t, ctx, resp)
		})
	}

	var preparedComment *issues_model.Comment
	run("prepare", func(t *testing.T, ctx *context.Context, resp *httptest.ResponseRecorder) {
		comment, err := pull.CreateCodeComment(ctx, pr.Issue.Poster, ctx.Repo.GitRepo, pr.Issue, 1, 0, "content", "", false, 0, pr.HeadCommitID, nil)
		require.NoError(t, err)

		comment.Invalidated = true
		err = issues_model.UpdateCommentInvalidate(ctx, comment)
		require.NoError(t, err)

		preparedComment = comment
	})
	require.NotNil(t, preparedComment)

	run("diff with outdated", func(t *testing.T, ctx *context.Context, resp *httptest.ResponseRecorder) {
		ctx.Data["ShowOutdatedComments"] = true
		renderConversation(ctx, preparedComment, "diff")
		assert.Contains(t, resp.Body.String(), `<div class="content comment-container"`)
	})
	run("diff without outdated", func(t *testing.T, ctx *context.Context, resp *httptest.ResponseRecorder) {
		ctx.Data["ShowOutdatedComments"] = false
		renderConversation(ctx, preparedComment, "diff")
		assert.Contains(t, resp.Body.String(), `conversation-not-existing`)
	})
	run("timeline with outdated", func(t *testing.T, ctx *context.Context, resp *httptest.ResponseRecorder) {
		ctx.Data["ShowOutdatedComments"] = true
		renderConversation(ctx, preparedComment, "timeline")
		assert.Contains(t, resp.Body.String(), `<div id="code-comments-`)
	})
	run("timeline is not affected by ShowOutdatedComments=false", func(t *testing.T, ctx *context.Context, resp *httptest.ResponseRecorder) {
		ctx.Data["ShowOutdatedComments"] = false
		renderConversation(ctx, preparedComment, "timeline")
		assert.Contains(t, resp.Body.String(), `<div id="code-comments-`)
	})
	run("diff non-existing review", func(t *testing.T, ctx *context.Context, resp *httptest.ResponseRecorder) {
		err := db.TruncateBeans(t.Context(), &issues_model.Review{})
		assert.NoError(t, err)
		ctx.Data["ShowOutdatedComments"] = true
		renderConversation(ctx, preparedComment, "diff")
		assert.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, resp.Code)
		assert.NotContains(t, resp.Body.String(), `status-page-500`)
	})
	run("timeline non-existing review", func(t *testing.T, ctx *context.Context, resp *httptest.ResponseRecorder) {
		err := db.TruncateBeans(t.Context(), &issues_model.Review{})
		assert.NoError(t, err)
		ctx.Data["ShowOutdatedComments"] = true
		renderConversation(ctx, preparedComment, "timeline")
		assert.Equal(t, http.StatusOK, resp.Code)
		assert.NotContains(t, resp.Body.String(), `status-page-500`)
	})
}

package pull_test

func TestDismissReview(t *testing.T) {
	assert.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())

	pull := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.PullRequest{})
	assert.NoError(t, pull.LoadIssue(t.Context()))
	issue := pull.Issue
	assert.NoError(t, issue.LoadRepo(t.Context()))
	reviewer := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 1})
	review, err := issues_model.CreateReview(t.Context(), issues_model.CreateReviewOptions{
		Issue:    issue,
		Reviewer: reviewer,
		Type:     issues_model.ReviewTypeReject,
	})

	assert.NoError(t, err)
	issue.IsClosed = true
	pull.HasMerged = false
	assert.NoError(t, issues_model.UpdateIssueCols(t.Context(), issue, "is_closed"))
	assert.NoError(t, pull.UpdateCols(t.Context(), "has_merged"))
	_, err = pull_service.DismissReview(t.Context(), review.ID, issue.RepoID, "", &user_model.User{}, false, false)
	assert.Error(t, err)
	assert.True(t, pull_service.IsErrDismissRequestOnClosedPR(err))

	pull.HasMerged = true
	pull.Issue.IsClosed = false
	assert.NoError(t, issues_model.UpdateIssueCols(t.Context(), issue, "is_closed"))
	assert.NoError(t, pull.UpdateCols(t.Context(), "has_merged"))
	_, err = pull_service.DismissReview(t.Context(), review.ID, issue.RepoID, "", &user_model.User{}, false, false)
	assert.Error(t, err)
	assert.True(t, pull_service.IsErrDismissRequestOnClosedPR(err))
}

// fileLines returns "l1\n".."lN\n" with the given lines replaced
func fileLines(n int, replace map[int]string) string {
	var sb strings.Builder
	for i := 1; i <= n; i++ {
		if s, ok := replace[i]; ok {
			sb.WriteString(s + "\n")
		} else {
			fmt.Fprintf(&sb, "l%d\n", i)
		}
	}
	return sb.String()
}

func TestPullReviewRangeComment(t *testing.T) {
	onGiteaRun(t, func(t *testing.T, u *url.URL) {
		user2 := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: 2})
		repo, err := repo_service.CreateRepositoryDirectly(t.Context(), user2, user2, repo_service.CreateRepoOptions{
			Name:             "test_range",
			AutoInit:         true,
			Readme:           "Default",
			ObjectFormatName: git.Sha1ObjectFormat.Name(),
			DefaultBranch:    "master",
		}, true)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		writeFile := func(branch, newBranch, content string) {
			_, err := files_service.ChangeRepoFiles(t.Context(), repo, user2, &files_service.ChangeRepoFilesOptions{
				OldBranch: branch,
				NewBranch: newBranch,
				Files:     []*files_service.ChangeRepoFile{{Operation: "update", TreePath: "README.md", ContentReader: strings.NewReader(content)}},
			})
			require.NoError(t, err)
		}
		// lines 2 and 13 of 14 change, so the diff has two hunks: new lines 1-5 and 10-14
		writeFile("master", "", fileLines(14, nil))
		writeFile("master", "range-branch", fileLines(14, map[int]string{2: "X2", 13: "X13"}))

		session := loginUser(t, "user2")
		testPullCreate(t, session, "user2", "test_range", false, "master", "range-branch", "Range PR")
		pr := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.PullRequest{BaseRepoID: repo.ID, HeadBranch: "range-branch"})
		require.NoError(t, pr.LoadIssue(t.Context()))
		commentURL := fmt.Sprintf("/user2/test_range/pulls/%d/files/reviews/comments", pr.Issue.Index)

		post := func(t *testing.T, origin, side, startLine, line string, status int) *HTMLDoc {
			req := NewRequestWithValues(t, "POST", commentURL, map[string]string{
				"origin":        origin,
				"content":       "```suggestion\nnew\n```",
				"side":          side,
				"start_line":    startLine,
				"line":          line,
				"path":          "README.md",
				"single_review": "true",
			})
			resp := session.MakeRequest(t, req, status)
			if status != http.StatusOK {
				return nil
			}
			return NewHTMLParser(t, resp.Body)
		}

		for _, origin := range []string{"diff", "timeline"} {
			t.Run("AC1 AC5 range on lines 1-3 from "+origin, func(t *testing.T) {
				doc := post(t, origin, "proposed", "1", "3", http.StatusOK)
				assert.Equal(t, "Lines 1–3", strings.TrimSpace(doc.Find(".code-comment-range").First().Text()))
				markup := doc.Find(".render-content.markup[data-suggestion-original]").Last()
				assert.Equal(t, "l1\nX2\nl3", markup.AttrOr("data-suggestion-original", ""))
			})
		}

		t.Run("AC3 one-line range is a single-line comment", func(t *testing.T) {
			doc := post(t, "diff", "proposed", "11", "11", http.StatusOK)
			assert.Equal(t, 0, doc.Find(".code-comment-range").Length())
			comment := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Comment{IssueID: pr.IssueID, Type: issues_model.CommentTypeCode, Line: 11})
			assert.EqualValues(t, 0, comment.RangeStartLine())
		})

		t.Run("AC12 invalid ranges are refused", func(t *testing.T) {
			before := unittest.GetCount(t, &issues_model.Comment{IssueID: pr.IssueID, Type: issues_model.CommentTypeCode})
			post(t, "diff", "proposed", "4", "3", http.StatusBadRequest)  // start after end
			post(t, "diff", "previous", "1", "3", http.StatusBadRequest)  // old side
			post(t, "diff", "proposed", "4", "11", http.StatusBadRequest) // two hunks
			post(t, "diff", "proposed", "7", "8", http.StatusBadRequest)  // between hunks, no hunk at all
			assert.Equal(t, before, unittest.GetCount(t, &issues_model.Comment{IssueID: pr.IssueID, Type: issues_model.CommentTypeCode}))
		})

		gitRepo, err := gitrepo.OpenRepository(t.Context(), repo)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		defer gitRepo.Close()
		invalidate := func(t *testing.T) {
			require.NoError(t, pull_service.InvalidateCodeComments(t.Context(), issues_model.PullRequestList{pr}, user2, repo, gitRepo, "range-branch"))
		}
		post(t, "diff", "proposed", "", "2", http.StatusOK) // AC13: a single-line comment on line 2
		ranged := func() []*issues_model.Comment {
			all, err := issues_model.FindComments(t.Context(), &issues_model.FindCommentsOptions{IssueID: pr.IssueID, Type: issues_model.CommentTypeCode})
			require.NoError(t, err)
			var cs []*issues_model.Comment
			for _, c := range all {
				if c.RangeStartLine() > 0 || c.Line == 2 {
					cs = append(cs, c)
				}
			}
			return cs
		}

		t.Run("AC8 a change after the range keeps it current", func(t *testing.T) {
			writeFile("range-branch", "", fileLines(14, map[int]string{2: "X2", 13: "Y13"}))
			invalidate(t)
			for _, c := range ranged() {
				assert.False(t, c.Invalidated, "comment on line %d", c.Line)
			}
		})

		t.Run("AC7 AC13 a change inside the range makes it outdated", func(t *testing.T) {
			writeFile("range-branch", "", fileLines(14, map[int]string{2: "Y2", 13: "Y13"}))
			invalidate(t)
			cs := ranged()
			require.Len(t, cs, 3) // two range comments and the single-line one
			for _, c := range cs {
				assert.True(t, c.Invalidated, "comment on line %d", c.Line)
			}
		})
	})
}

import {html, htmlEscape, htmlRaw} from '../utils/html.ts';
import {svgRaw} from '../svg.ts';
import {animateOnce, queryElems, showElem} from '../utils/dom.ts';
import Toastify from 'toastify-js'; // don't use "async import", because when network error occurs, the "async import" also fails and nothing is shown
import type {Intent} from '../types.ts';
import type {SvgName} from '../svg.ts';
import type {Options} from 'toastify-js';
import type StartToastifyInstance from 'toastify-js';

export type Toast = ReturnType<typeof StartToastifyInstance>;

type ToastLevels = {
  [intent in Intent]: {
    icon: SvgName,
    background: string,
    duration: number,
  }
};

const levels: ToastLevels = {
  info: {
    icon: 'octicon-check',
    background: 'var(--color-green)',
    duration: 2500,
  },
  warning: {
    icon: 'gitea-exclamation',
    background: 'var(--color-orange)',
    duration: -1, // requires dismissal to hide
  },
  error: {
    icon: 'gitea-exclamation',
    background: 'var(--color-red)',
    duration: -1, // requires dismissal to hide
  },
};

type ToastOpts = {
  useHtmlBody?: boolean,
  preventDuplicates?: boolean | string,
} & Options;

type ToastifyElement = HTMLElement & {_giteaToastifyInstance?: Toast};

/** See https://github.com/apvarun/toastify-js#api for options */
function showToast(message: string, level: Intent, {gravity, position, duration, useHtmlBody, preventDuplicates = true, ...other}: ToastOpts = {}): Toast | null {
  const parent = document.querySelector('.ui.dimmer.active') ?? document.body;
  const duplicateKey = preventDuplicates ? (typeof preventDuplicates === 'string' ? preventDuplicates : `${level}-${message}`) : '';

  // prevent showing duplicate toasts with the same level and message, and give visual feedback for end users
  if (preventDuplicates) {
    const toastEl = parent.querySelector(`:scope > .toastify.on[data-toast-unique-key="${CSS.escape(duplicateKey)}"]`);
    if (toastEl) {
      const toastDupNumEl = toastEl.querySelector('.toast-duplicate-number')!;
      showElem(toastDupNumEl);
      toastDupNumEl.textContent = String(Number(toastDupNumEl.textContent) + 1);
      animateOnce(toastDupNumEl, 'pulse-1p5-200');
      return null;
    }
  }

  const {icon, background, duration: levelDuration} = levels[level ?? 'info'];
  const bodyHtml = useHtmlBody ? message : htmlEscape(message);
  const toast = Toastify({
    selector: parent,
    text: html`
      <div class='toast-icon'>${svgRaw(icon)}</div>
      <div class='toast-body'><span class="toast-duplicate-number tw-hidden">1</span>${htmlRaw(bodyHtml)}</div>
      <button class='btn toast-close'>${svgRaw('octicon-x')}</button>
    `,
    escapeMarkup: false,
    gravity: gravity ?? 'top',
    position: position ?? 'center',
    duration: duration ?? levelDuration,
    style: {background},
    ...other,
  });

  toast.showToast();
  const el = toast.toastElement as ToastifyElement;

// InvalidateCodeComments will lookup the prs for code comments which got invalidated by change
func InvalidateCodeComments(ctx context.Context, prs issues_model.PullRequestList, doer *user_model.User, repo *repo_model.Repository, gitRepo *git.Repository, branch string) error {
	if len(prs) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	issueIDs := prs.GetIssueIDs()

	codeComments, err := db.Find[issues_model.Comment](ctx, issues_model.FindCommentsOptions{
		ListOptions: db.ListOptionsAll,
		Type:        issues_model.CommentTypeCode,
		Invalidated: optional.Some(false),
		IssueIDs:    issueIDs,
	})
	if err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("find code comments: %v", err)
	}
	var head *git.Commit
	headFiles := map[string]string{} // each file is read once per push, however many range comments it has
	for _, comment := range codeComments {
	tplConversationOutdated templates.TplName = "repo/diff/conversation_outdated"
	tplTimelineConversation templates.TplName = "repo/issue/view_content/conversation"
	tplNewComment           templates.TplName = "repo/diff/new_comment"
)

// RenderNewCodeCommentForm will render the form for creating a new review comment
func RenderNewCodeCommentForm(ctx *context.Context) {
	issue := GetActionIssue(ctx)
	if ctx.Written() {
		return
	}
	if !issue.IsPull {
		return
	}
	currentReview, err := issues_model.GetCurrentReview(ctx, ctx.Doer, issue)
	if err != nil && !issues_model.IsErrReviewNotExist(err) {
		ctx.ServerError("GetCurrentReview", err)
		return
	}
	ctx.Data["PageIsPullFiles"] = true
	ctx.Data["Issue"] = issue
	ctx.Data["CurrentReview"] = currentReview
	pullHeadCommitID, err := ctx.Repo.GitRepo.GetRefCommitID(issue.PullRequest.GetGitHeadRefName())
	if err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("GetRefCommitID", err)
		return
	}
	ctx.Data["AfterCommitID"] = pullHeadCommitID
	ctx.Data["IsAttachmentEnabled"] = setting.Attachment.Enabled
	if startLine, line := ctx.FormInt64("start_line"), ctx.FormInt64("line"); startLine > 0 && startLine < line {
		ctx.Data["RangeStartLine"], ctx.Data["RangeEndLine"] = startLine, line
	}
	upload.AddUploadContext(ctx, "comment")
	ctx.HTML(http.StatusOK, tplNewComment)
}

// CreateCodeComment will create a code comment including an pending review if required
func CreateCodeComment(ctx *context.Context) {
	form := web.GetForm(ctx).(*forms.CodeCommentForm)
	issue := GetActionIssue(ctx)
	if ctx.Written() {
		return
	}
	if !issue.IsPull {
		return
	}

	if ctx.HasError() {
		ctx.Flash.Error(ctx.GetErrMsg())
		ctx.Redirect(fmt.Sprintf("%s/pulls/%d/files", ctx.Repo.RepoLink, issue.Index))
		return
	}

	signedLine := form.Line
	if form.Side == "previous" {
		signedLine *= -1
	}

	startLine := form.StartLine
	if startLine == form.Line {
		startLine = 0 // a one-line range is a normal single-line comment
	}

	var attachments []string
	if setting.Attachment.Enabled {
		attachments = form.Files
	}

	comment, err := pull_service.CreateCodeComment(ctx,
		ctx.Doer,
		ctx.Repo.GitRepo,
		issue,
		signedLine,
		startLine,
		form.Content,
		form.TreePath,
		!form.SingleReview,
		form.Reply,
		form.LatestCommitID,
		attachments,
	)
	if errors.Is(err, pull_service.ErrCodeCommentRangeInvalid) {
		ctx.JSONError(ctx.Tr("repo.diff.comment.range_invalid"))
		return
	} else if err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("CreateCodeComment", err)
		return
	}

	if comment == nil {
		log.Trace("Comment not created: %-v #%d[%d]", ctx.Repo.Repository, issue.Index, issue.ID)
		ctx.Redirect(fmt.Sprintf("%s/pulls/%d/files", ctx.Repo.RepoLink, issue.Index))
		return
	}

	log.Trace("Comment created: %-v #%d[%d] Comment[%d]", ctx.Repo.Repository, issue.Index, issue.ID, comment.ID)

# PR #177 (#158): raise new-code coverage + fix AC11 e2e check

## Context
SonarQube reports 29.2% coverage on new code (80% required). Coverage comes only from
`make test-backend -coverprofile` (per-package Go unit tests, no `-coverpkg`, `tests/integration`
excluded) and vitest lcov (`sonar-project.properties`, `pull-db-tests.yml`). So the PR's
integration test (`tests/integration/pull_review_range_test.go`) and e2e test count for nothing;
most new lines in `services/pull/review.go`, `routers/web/repo/pull_review.go`,
`models/issues/comment.go` and `web_src/js/features/repo-diff-range.ts` are uncovered.
Gitar also flagged that the AC11 e2e step passes on the stale AC15 toast.

Work on branch `feat/issue-158-multiline-suggestions` (local == origin at dfaf21a05f). Switch to it first.
Expected values come from the #158 ACs and the fixture repo's actual git content (PR 2 = repo1
`branch2` vs merge base `4a35743`; README.md new lines 1-6 are one hunk:
`# repo1`, ``, `Description for repo1`, ``, `And change for branch2`, `and a second one`).

## Changes

### 1. e2e fix — `tests/e2e/pr-suggest-change.test.ts` (AC11 step)
Apply Gitar's fix: click `.toastify .toast-close`, assert message count 0, do old-2 → shift new-4,
assert message visible again, assert `tr.range-selected` count 0. Drop the `.last()`.

### 2. Go: `services/pull/review_range_test.go` (extend, package `pull`, has TestMain)
New `TestCreateCodeCommentRange` using `unittest.PrepareTestEnv`, PR 2, `gitrepo.OpenRepository`:
- range 3..5 on README.md, single review → no error, `RangeStartLine()==3`,
  `RangeOriginalLines()` == `["Description for repo1", "", "And change for branch2"]` (AC1/AC4)
- invalid ranges → `ErrCodeCommentRangeInvalid`, no comment created (AC12):
  start == line, start > line, old side (line < 0), start beyond hunk (e.g. 0 < start, line 9 outside diff)
- reply with a different start line to that thread → `ErrCodeCommentRangeInvalid`; reply with 0
  inherits the thread's start (existing comment in `createCodeComment`)
- `InvalidateCodeComments(..., "branch2")` → range comment stays valid (AC8: unchanged text);
  `InvalidateCodeComments(..., "master")` → invalidated (master README has only 3 lines, AC7)
Covers `CreateCodeComment`/`createCodeComment` range paths, `InvalidateCodeComments` head-file
loop, `checkRangeInvalidation`. Reuse existing `TestRangeChanged` as is.

### 3. Go: `routers/web/repo/pull_review_test.go`
Add `TestCreateCodeCommentRange` / `TestRenderNewCodeCommentFormRange` with `contexttest.MockContext`
(pattern of `TestRenderConversation`, `web.SetForm` like `issue_label_test.go`):
- `RenderNewCodeCommentForm` with `?start_line=2&line=4` → `ctx.Data["RangeStartLine"]==2`, `RangeEndLine==4`; `start_line=4&line=4` → unset
- `CreateCodeComment` with `forms.CodeCommentForm{StartLine: 4, Line: 3, Side: "proposed", ...}` → 400 JSON with the range_invalid message
- `StartLine == Line` → saved as single-line comment (`RangeStartLine()==0`, AC3)

### 4. Go: `models/issues/comment_test.go` / `comment_suggestion_test.go`
- `CreateComment` with `Type: CommentTypeCode, StartLine: 2, LineNum: 4` → reloaded bean `RangeStartLine()==2`; without StartLine → 0 (nil metadata branch)
- `RangeOriginalLines` false cases: no start, `Line < start`

### 5. JS: `web_src/js/features/repo-diff-range.test.ts`
`vi.mock('../modules/toast.ts')`, call `initDiffRangeSelect()` once, build a unified-diff table
inside `<div data-range-invalid="msg">` with `td.lines-num-new`/`lines-num-old` cells, dispatch events:
- click 18, shift-click 20 → `tr.range-selected` 3 rows, `getSelectedRange(last)` = {start 18, end 20}; `getSelectedRange(other row)` null (AC1)
- Enter / Shift+Enter keydown does the same (AC14); other keys ignored
- old-side anchor + shift-click new → `showErrorToast('msg')`, selection cleared (AC11)

func TestCreateComment(t *testing.T) {
	assert.NoError(t, unittest.PrepareTestDatabase())

	issue := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{})
	repo := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &repo_model.Repository{ID: issue.RepoID})
	doer := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &user_model.User{ID: repo.OwnerID})

	now := time.Now().Unix()
	comment, err := issues_model.CreateComment(t.Context(), &issues_model.CreateCommentOptions{
		Type:    issues_model.CommentTypeComment,
		Doer:    doer,
		Repo:    repo,
		Issue:   issue,
		Content: "Hello",
	})
	assert.NoError(t, err)
	then := time.Now().Unix()

	assert.Equal(t, issues_model.CommentTypeComment, comment.Type)
	assert.Equal(t, "Hello", comment.Content)
	assert.Equal(t, issue.ID, comment.IssueID)
	assert.Equal(t, doer.ID, comment.PosterID)
	unittest.AssertInt64InRange(t, now, then, int64(comment.CreatedUnix))
	unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, comment) // assert actually added to DB

	updatedIssue := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Issue{ID: issue.ID})
	unittest.AssertInt64InRange(t, now, then, int64(updatedIssue.UpdatedUnix))
}

package issues_test

import (
	"testing"

	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
	"gitea.dev/modules/optional"

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
)

func TestCommentSuggestionOriginalLine(t *testing.T) {
	const header = "diff --git a/main.go b/main.go\n--- a/main.go\n+++ b/main.go\n@@ -1,3 +1,3 @@\n"
	cases := []struct {
		name     string
		typ      issues_model.CommentType
		line     int64
		patch    string
		expected optional.Option[string]
	}{
		{"added line keeps indentation", issues_model.CommentTypeCode, 3, header + " package main\n-\treturn nil\n+\treturn err", optional.Some("\treturn err")},
		{"context line", issues_model.CommentTypeCode, 2, header + " package main\n func main() {}", optional.Some("func main() {}")},
		{"trailing newline in patch", issues_model.CommentTypeCode, 2, header + " package main\n+x := 1\n", optional.Some("x := 1")},
		{"blank context line", issues_model.CommentTypeCode, 2, header + " package main\n ", optional.Some("")},
		{"CRLF kept", issues_model.CommentTypeCode, 1, header + "+foo\r", optional.Some("foo\r")},
		{"old side is not supported", issues_model.CommentTypeCode, -2, header + " package main\n-\treturn nil", optional.None[string]()},
		{"removed line on new side is inconsistent", issues_model.CommentTypeCode, 2, header + " package main\n-gone", optional.None[string]()},
		{"empty patch", issues_model.CommentTypeCode, 2, "", optional.None[string]()},
		{"header only", issues_model.CommentTypeCode, 2, header, optional.None[string]()},
		{"not a code comment", issues_model.CommentTypeComment, 2, header + "+x", optional.None[string]()},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			comment := &issues_model.Comment{Type: c.typ, Line: c.line, Patch: c.patch}
			assert.Equal(t, c.expected, comment.SuggestionOriginalLine())
		})
	}

// CreateCodeComment creates a comment on the code line
func CreateCodeComment(ctx context.Context, doer *user_model.User, gitRepo *git.Repository, issue *issues_model.Issue, line, startLine int64, content, treePath string, pendingReview bool, replyReviewID int64, latestCommitID string, attachments []string) (*issues_model.Comment, error) {
	var (
		existsReview bool
		err          error
	)

	// CreateCodeComment() is used for:
	// - Single comments
	// - Comments that are part of a review
	// - Comments that reply to an existing review

	if !pendingReview && replyReviewID != 0 {
		// It's not part of a review; maybe a reply to a review comment or a single comment.
		// Check if there are reviews for that line already; if there are, this is a reply
		if existsReview, err = issues_model.ReviewExists(ctx, issue, treePath, line); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
	}

	// Comments that are replies don't require a review header to show up in the issue view
	if !pendingReview && existsReview {
		if err = issue.LoadRepo(ctx); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}

		comment, err := createCodeComment(ctx,
			doer,
			issue.Repo,
			issue,
			content,
			treePath,
			line,
			startLine,
			replyReviewID,
			attachments,
		)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}

		mentions, err := issues_model.FindAndUpdateIssueMentions(ctx, issue, doer, comment.Content)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}

		notify_service.CreateIssueComment(ctx, doer, issue.Repo, issue, comment, mentions)

		return comment, nil
	}

	review, err := issues_model.GetCurrentReview(ctx, doer, issue)
	if err != nil {
		if !issues_model.IsErrReviewNotExist(err) {
			return nil, err
		}

		if review, err = issues_model.CreateReview(ctx, issues_model.CreateReviewOptions{
			Type:     issues_model.ReviewTypePending,
			Reviewer: doer,
			Issue:    issue,
			Official: false,
			CommitID: latestCommitID,
		}); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
	}

	comment, err := createCodeComment(ctx,
		doer,
		issue.Repo,
		issue,
		content,
		treePath,
		line,
		startLine,
		review.ID,
		attachments,
	)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}

	if !pendingReview && !existsReview {
		// Submit the review we've just created so the comment shows up in the issue view
		if _, _, err = SubmitReview(ctx, doer, gitRepo, issue, issues_model.ReviewTypeComment, "", latestCommitID, nil); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
	}

	// NOTICE: if it's a pending review the notifications will not be fired until user submit review.

	return comment, nil
}

// createCodeComment creates a plain code comment at the specified line / path
func createCodeComment(ctx context.Context, doer *user_model.User, repo *repo_model.Repository, issue *issues_model.Issue, content, treePath string, line, startLine, reviewID int64, attachments []string) (*issues_model.Comment, error) {
	if startLine != 0 && (line <= 0 || startLine < 0 || startLine >= line) {
		return nil, ErrCodeCommentRangeInvalid // ranges are new-side only and end after they start
	}
	var commitID, patch string
	if err := issue.LoadPullRequest(ctx); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("LoadPullRequest: %w", err)
	}
	pr := issue.PullRequest
	if err := pr.LoadBaseRepo(ctx); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("LoadBaseRepo: %w", err)
	}
	gitRepo, closer, err := gitrepo.RepositoryFromContextOrOpen(ctx, pr.BaseRepo)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("RepositoryFromContextOrOpen: %w", err)
	}
	defer closer.Close()

	invalidated := false
	head := pr.GetGitHeadRefName()
	if line > 0 {
		if reviewID != 0 {
			first, err := issues_model.FindComments(ctx, &issues_model.FindCommentsOptions{
				ReviewID: reviewID,
				Line:     line,
				TreePath: treePath,
				Type:     issues_model.CommentTypeCode,
				ListOptions: db.ListOptions{
					PageSize: 1,
					Page:     1,
				},
			})
			if err == nil && len(first) > 0 {
				commitID = first[0].CommitSHA
				invalidated = first[0].Invalidated
				patch = first[0].Patch
				if startLine == 0 {
					startLine = first[0].RangeStartLine() // a reply joins its thread's range
				} else if startLine != first[0].RangeStartLine() {
					return nil, ErrCodeCommentRangeInvalid
				}
			} else if err != nil && !issues_model.IsErrCommentNotExist(err) {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("Find first comment for %d line %d path %s. Error: %w", reviewID, line, treePath, err)
			} else {
				review, err := issues_model.GetReviewByID(ctx, reviewID)
				if err == nil && len(review.CommitID) > 0 {
					head = review.CommitID
				} else if err != nil && !issues_model.IsErrReviewNotExist(err) {
					return nil, fmt.Errorf("GetReviewByID %d. Error: %w", reviewID, err)
				}
			}
		}

		if len(commitID) == 0 {
			// FIXME validate treePath
			// Get latest commit referencing the commented line
			// No need for get commit for base branch changes
			commit, err := lineBlame(ctx, pr.BaseRepo, gitRepo, head, treePath, uint(line))
			if err == nil {
				commitID = commit.ID.String()
			} else if !isErrBlameNotFoundOrNotEnoughLines(err) {
				return nil, fmt.Errorf("LineBlame[%s, %s, %s, %d]: %w", pr.GetGitHeadRefName(), gitRepo.Path, treePath, line, err)
			}
		}
	}

	// Only fetch diff if comment is review comment
	if len(patch) == 0 && reviewID != 0 {
		headCommitID, err := gitRepo.GetRefCommitID(pr.GetGitHeadRefName())
		if err != nil {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("GetRefCommitID[%s]: %w", pr.GetGitHeadRefName(), err)
		}
		if len(commitID) == 0 {
			commitID = headCommitID
		}

		window := setting.UI.CodeCommentLines
		if startLine > 0 {
			window = math.MaxInt32 // shortcut: stores the whole hunk up to the range end, not just the range plus context; trim it if long hunks bloat the conversation snippet
		}
		patch, err = git.GetFileDiffCutAroundLine(
			gitRepo, pr.MergeBase, headCommitID, treePath,
			int64((&issues_model.Comment{Line: line}).UnsignedLine()), line < 0, window,
		)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		if startLine > 0 {
			if _, ok := issues_model.PatchLastNewLines(patch, int(line-startLine+1)); !ok {

func TestCreateCodeCommentRange(t *testing.T) {
	unittest.PrepareTestEnv(t)
	pr := unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.PullRequest{ID: 2})
	require.NoError(t, pr.LoadIssue(t.Context()))
	require.NoError(t, pr.Issue.LoadRepo(t.Context()))
	require.NoError(t, pr.Issue.LoadPoster(t.Context()))
	gitRepo, err := gitrepo.OpenRepository(t.Context(), pr.Issue.Repo)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	defer gitRepo.Close()
	create := func(line, startLine, replyReviewID int64) (*issues_model.Comment, error) {
		return CreateCodeComment(t.Context(), pr.Issue.Poster, gitRepo, pr.Issue, line, startLine, "range", "README.md", false, replyReviewID, pr.HeadCommitID, nil)
	}
	countCodeComments := func() int {
		return unittest.GetCount(t, &issues_model.Comment{IssueID: pr.IssueID, Type: issues_model.CommentTypeCode})
	}

	// #158 AC1 AC4: lines 3-5 store their start and the text the reviewer saw
	comment, err := create(5, 3, 0)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	assert.EqualValues(t, 3, comment.RangeStartLine())
	lines, ok := comment.RangeOriginalLines()
	assert.True(t, ok)
	assert.Equal(t, []string{"Description for repo1", "", "And change for branch2"}, lines)

	t.Run("AC12 invalid ranges are refused", func(t *testing.T) {
		before := countCodeComments()
		for _, c := range []struct{ name string; line, start int64 }{
			{"start equals end", 4, 4},
			{"start after end", 3, 4},
			{"old side", -3, 1},
			{"negative start", 4, -1},
			{"outside the diff", 9, 7},
		} {
			_, err := create(c.line, c.start, 0)
			assert.ErrorIs(t, err, ErrCodeCommentRangeInvalid, c.name)
		}
		assert.Equal(t, before, countCodeComments())
	})

	t.Run("a reply joins its thread's range", func(t *testing.T) {
		_, err := create(5, 4, comment.ReviewID)
		assert.ErrorIs(t, err, ErrCodeCommentRangeInvalid) // another start on the same thread
		reply, err := create(5, 0, comment.ReviewID)
		require.NoError(t, err)
		assert.EqualValues(t, 3, reply.RangeStartLine())
	})

	invalidated := func(t *testing.T, branch string) bool {
		require.NoError(t, InvalidateCodeComments(t.Context(), issues_model.PullRequestList{pr}, pr.Issue.Poster, pr.Issue.Repo, gitRepo, branch))
		return unittest.AssertExistsAndLoadBean(t, &issues_model.Comment{ID: comment.ID}).Invalidated
	}
	// #158 AC8: the branch head still has the range's text
	assert.False(t, invalidated(t, "branch2"))
	// #158 AC7: master's README.md ends at line 3, so lines 4-5 of the range are gone
	assert.True(t, invalidated(t, "master"))
}
'''
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

vi.mock('../modules/toast.ts', () => ({showErrorToast: vi.fn()}));

// a unified diff with both line-number cells, inside the element that carries the refusal message
function diffRows(html: string) {
  document.body.innerHTML = `<div data-range-invalid="msg"><table><tbody>${html}</tbody></table></div>`;
  return Array.from(document.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('tr'));
}

function diffRow(cls: string, oldLine: string, newLine: string) {
  return `<tr class="${cls}"><td class="lines-num lines-num-old" data-line-num="${oldLine}"></td><td class="lines-num lines-num-new" data-line-num="${newLine}"></td></tr>`;
}

const cell = (side: 'old' | 'new', line: number) => document.querySelector<HTMLElement>(`td.lines-num-${side}[data-line-num="${line}"]`)!;
const click = (el: HTMLElement, shiftKey = false) => el.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('click', {bubbles: true, shiftKey}));
const press = (el: HTMLElement, key: string, shiftKey = false) => el.dispatchEvent(new KeyboardEvent('keydown', {bubbles: true, key, shiftKey}));
const selectedLines = () => Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('tr.range-selected'), (tr) => tr.querySelector('.lines-num-new')!.getAttribute('data-line-num'));

initDiffRangeSelect();

const hunk = diffRow('same-code', '18', '18') + diffRow('del-code', '19', '') + diffRow('add-code', '', '19') + diffRow('same-code', '20', '20');

test('click then shift-click selects a range', () => {
  const trs = diffRows(hunk);
  click(cell('new', 18));
  expect(selectedLines()).toEqual(['18']);
  click(cell('new', 20), true);
  // #158 AC1: lines 18-20, the removed line is not part of the range
  expect(selectedLines()).toEqual(['18', '19', '20']);
  expect(getSelectedRange(trs[3])).toEqual({rows: [trs[0], trs[2], trs[3]], start: 18, end: 20});
  expect(getSelectedRange(trs[2])).toBeNull(); // the form opens on the range's last line only
});

test('Enter and Shift+Enter select a range from the keyboard', () => {
  diffRows(hunk);
  press(cell('new', 19), 'Enter');
  press(cell('new', 20), 'a', true); // other keys do nothing
  expect(selectedLines()).toEqual(['19']);
  press(cell('new', 20), 'Enter', true);
  // #158 AC14
  expect(selectedLines()).toEqual(['19', '20']);
});

test('one line is not a range', () => {
  const trs = diffRows(hunk);
  click(cell('new', 18));
  // #158 AC3
  expect(getSelectedRange(trs[0])).toBeNull();
});

test('a range across sides or hunks is refused', () => {
  diffRows(hunk + diffRow('tag-code', '', '') + diffRow('same-code', '40', '40'));
  // #158 AC11: old side to new side
  click(cell('old', 18));
  expect(selectedLines()).toEqual([]);
  click(cell('new', 20), true);
  expect(showErrorToast).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith('msg');
  expect(selectedLines()).toEqual([]);

  // #158 AC10: across a hunk header
  vi.mocked(showErrorToast).mockClear();
  click(cell('new', 18));

Review a change like the senior developer who will be paged when it breaks.
Order of importance: correct, safe, holds under load, tested, fast, lean.
Lean still matters: every extra line must be read, tested and fixed later.
This is a report the user asked for, so give it in full.

## 1. Understand first

- Review what the user names: uncommitted or staged changes, a branch, a PR
  link, or files. Nothing named: the uncommitted changes, or the last commit
  if there are none.
- Read the diff, then the code it touches: callers of every changed function,
  the functions it calls, the tests, the README.
- Trace the real flow: where data comes in, what is stored, what goes out.
- A change can break code it does not touch. When a signature, return value
  or behavior changes, grep every caller.
- Find the expected load in the repo (README, deploy config): one person
  running a script, or many users and processes at once. Judge scale against
  that, and say which load you assumed.

## 2. Look for

1. **Bug:** wrong result, crash, missed edge case (empty, zero, last item,
   rounding, time zones), a caller broken by the change, a fix applied in one
   caller while the shared function stays broken.
2. **Risk:** security holes (injection, weak randomness, secrets, missing
   checks on input from users), data loss (errors swallowed, writes in the
   wrong order, no transaction).
3. **Scale:** fine for one user, wrong for many: check-then-write races, the
   same work done by every process, memory or lists that only grow, a query
   per item, O(n^2) on big input, per-process state that must be shared.
4. **Missing test:** risky new logic (a branch, a parser, money, security,
   data writes, a bug fix) with no test that fails when it breaks. One good
   test, not coverage.
5. **Speed:** big slowdowns are problems. Small wins (work repeated in a hot
   loop) are suggestions; some software counts every millisecond.
6. **Lean:** code that should not exist or should be smaller.
   - delete: dead code, unused options, speculative features
   - reuse: the repo already has this helper (name the path)
   - stdlib / native: the standard library or platform already does it; a
     new dependency for a few lines
   - yagni: abstraction with one implementation, config nobody sets
   - merge: near-copies that must change together
   - split: one function doing several unrelated jobs, so it is hard to read
     or test. Split by job, never by line count, and never into helpers that
     exist only to make a function shorter.

## 3. Check before you report

- Every finding needs a concrete case: "this input or situation leads to this
  wrong result". No case, no finding.
- Re-read the lines and confirm: the caller exists, the value can really be
  empty, the code really is unused.
- A shortcut marked with a `shortcut:` (or older `ponytail:`) comment that names its limit is a
  decision, not a finding, unless the expected load already crosses it.
- Propose the smallest fix that works. Prefer fixes that delete code. Never
  add layers, frameworks or config the problem does not need.
- No style taste, no "consider", no vague worries.

## 4. Output

Very simple English: short sentences, everyday words. Explain a technical
term the first time you use it. The reader may never have seen this code.

Start with `What this change does:` in two or three sentences.

Then the findings in three groups, skip empty groups:
- **Must fix:** bug, security, data loss, breaks at the expected load.
- **Should fix:** risky code without a test, real slowness, duplication, a
  function that mixes jobs, code that should not exist.
- **Nice to have:** small speed-ups, shorter forms.

Number findings across all groups, so the user can say "fix 2 and 5".
Every finding has all four parts, each one or two short sentences:

2. **Orders land on the wrong day** (`billing/close_day.py:L40-52`)
   - **What this is:** At midnight this job closes the day and bills all orders of that day.
   - **Problem:** It takes "today" from the server clock, which runs in UTC. An order placed
     at 00:30 in Berlin is billed on the day before.
   - **Fix:** Compute the day once in the shop's time zone:
     `datetime.now(ZoneInfo("Europe/Berlin")).date()`. One line, nothing else changes.
   - **If we skip it:** Late orders show the wrong date, and accounting fixes them by hand.

End with:
- `Verdict: Ship.` or `Verdict: fix 1 and 3 first.`
- `Lean: -<N> lines possible.` when lean findings exist.
- `Not checked:` one line, if something mattered and you could not check it.

Nothing found: `What this change does:`, then `Looks good. Ship.` and one line
on what you checked.

Lists findings, changes no code.

_**Agent (claude-opus-5-5 2026-11-17 03:39:11Z)**_

What this change does: It adds tests only. There are Go unit tests for multi-line code comment ranges in three packages (model, service, web handler) and vitest tests for line selection in the browser. It also fixes the AC11 e2e check so it can no longer pass on the toast left over from AC15. No product code changed.

I checked each new test against the code it calls (`CreateCodeComment`, `createCodeComment`, `InvalidateCodeComments`, the web handlers, `selectLine`). Each one fails if the behavior it names breaks. For example, if the router stopped turning start == end into a single-line comment, the AC3 router test would get a 400 and fail. Load assumed: a test suite run by CI.

**Nice to have**

1. **A refused range leaves an empty pending review behind** (`services/pull/review.go`, `CreateCodeComment`)
   - **What this is:** A pending review is a review the user has started but not submitted. "Add single comment" creates one first, then calls `createCodeComment`, which checks the range.
   - **Problem:** When the range is refused, the pending review created a moment earlier stays in the database with no comments. Your new AC12 test passes through this path but only counts comments, so it doesn't see this. The next comment reuses that review, so users will rarely notice. Upstream code has the same pattern for its other errors.
   - **Fix:** Move the cheap check (`startLine != 0 && (line <= 0 || startLine < 0 || startLine >= line)`) to the top of `CreateCodeComment`, before any review is created. The check that the range fits in one hunk needs the diff, so it has to stay where it is.
   - **If we skip it:** An empty pending review row may be left in the database. Nothing breaks.

2. **One test function can be a table row** (`models/issues/comment_suggestion_test.go`, `TestCommentRangeOriginalLinesNoRange`)
   - **What this is:** A new 8-line test that checks `RangeOriginalLines` returns false.
   - **Problem:** Its "start after end" case fits the existing table in `TestCommentSuggestionOriginalLineRange`: `{"start after end", 23, 22, patch, optional.None[string]()}`. Its "no metadata" case tests a path that never runs, because both callers only call `RangeOriginalLines` when a start line is set. Sonar already counts that line as covered.
   - **Fix:** Delete the function and add the one row.
   - **If we skip it:** You keep one extra test function to read.

Verdict: Ship.
Lean: about 7 lines could go.
Not checked: the real Sonar score, which only CI can produce. The e2e file passes with `--workers=1`; with parallel workers this container hits 10s timeouts.

```text
// CreateCodeComment creates a comment on the code line
func CreateCodeComment(ctx context.Context, doer *user_model.User, gitRepo *git.Repository, issue *issues_model.Issue, line, startLine int64, content, treePath string, pendingReview bool, replyReviewID int64, latestCommitID string, attachments []string) (*issues_model.Comment, error) {
	var (
		existsReview bool
		err          error
	)

	if startLine != 0 && (line <= 0 || startLine < 0 || startLine >= line) {
		return nil, ErrCodeCommentRangeInvalid // ranges are new-side only and end after they start; checked before a pending review is created
	}

	// CreateCodeComment() is used for:
	// - Single comments
	// - Comments that are part of a review
	// - Comments that reply to an existing review
	const patch = header + " l16\n l17\n l18\n+\tl19\n-old\n l20\n+l21\n l22"
	cases := []struct {
		name     string
		start    int64
		line     int64
		patch    string
		expected optional.Option[string]
	}{
		{"lines 18-22 in order, removed line skipped", 18, 22, patch, optional.Some("l18\n\tl19\nl20\nl21\nl22")},
		{"range reaching the hunk start", 16, 22, patch, optional.Some("l16\nl17\nl18\n\tl19\nl20\nl21\nl22")},
		{"range longer than the stored hunk", 15, 22, patch, optional.None[string]()},
		{"no newline at end of file marker", 21, 22, patch + "\n\\ No newline at end of file", optional.Some("l21\nl22")},
		{"empty patch", 18, 22, "", optional.None[string]()},
		{"start after end", 23, 22, patch, optional.None[string]()},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			comment := &issues_model.Comment{
				Type: issues_model.CommentTypeCode, Line: c.line, Patch: c.patch,
				CommentMetaData: &issues_model.CommentMetaData{StartLine: c.start},
			}
			assert.Equal(t, c.expected, comment.SuggestionOriginalLine())
		})
	}
}
```
</details></tool-use>

This is the same problem as the vue-tsc failure.

**Why it's 55.7%:** CI runs vitest on your branch merged with `main`. There, `main`'s new test `initSuggestChangeButton in a form` passes one element where this PR's code expects a list. At runtime that throws `TypeError: codeLines.map is not a function` at `repo-diff-suggestion.ts:68`. The `frontend-coverage` step in the `sonarqube` job then fails, and vitest writes no coverage file when a test fails. The scan still ran, but with Go coverage only, so every new TypeScript line counted as uncovered. That includes `repo-diff-range.ts`, which reaches 97% locally. Go coverage did arrive: `test-unit` passed.

**The fix is the one already staged:** `main` merged in, and line 124 of [repo-diff-suggestion.test.ts](web_src/js/features/repo-diff-suggestion.test.ts#L124) now passes `[element]`. Locally on the merged tree, vitest passes 24/24 for `repo-diff*` and `markup/suggestion`, and vue-tsc is clean. So the next scan should include JavaScript coverage again.

I can't promise it will reach 80%. A few new lines in `repo-diff.ts` and `repo-issue.ts` are only covered by e2e, which Sonar doesn't count. Every other new Go and TypeScript function is fully or mostly covered by unit tests. We'll know the real number after this push is scanned.
